plate_findings.evidence: Caption states that inflammatory infiltration of the fascia is composed of lymphocytes, plasma cells, macrophages, and eosinophils; the arrow highlights a cell within the infiltrate.

panels.rationale: Whole-figure plate of 6 panels (A, B, C, D, E, F). A: Patient H&E section explicitly showing thickened fascia with moderate inflammatory infiltration in an article focused on juvenile eosinophilic fasciitis. B: High-magnification patient H&E section demonstrates an eosinophil-containing inflammatory infiltrate in the fascia, a characteristic pathology of eosinophilic fasciitis. C: Patient CD45 immunohistochemical section highlights the inflammatory leukocytes in a tissue section presented as representative eosinophilic fasciitis pathology. D: Patient CD163 immunohistochemical section demonstrates macrophages within the inflammatory infiltrate in representative eosinophilic fasciitis tissue. E: Patient CD138 immunohistochemical section highlights plasma cells in tissue presented as representative eosinophilic fasciitis pathology. F: Patient H&E section shows extension of eosinophilic fasciitis inflammation into muscle with mild perimysial inflammation, specifically marked by the arrow.

panels.figure_caption: Representative eosinophilic fasciitis pathology characteristics. A Hematoxylin and eosin (H&E) section (patient 4, magnification, × 40) showing fascia with underlying muscle. The fascia shows thickening and moderate inflammatory cell infiltration. B H&E section (patient 3, magnification, × 400) showing extensive infiltration of fascia by inflammatory cells composed of lymphocytes, plasma cells, macrophages, and eosinophils. C CD45 (leukocyte common antigen, LCA) immunohistochemical stain (patient 4, magnification, × 200) highlighting the inflammatory cells. D CD163 immunohistochemical stain (patient 4, magnification, × 200) highlights macrophages. E CD138 immunohistochemical stain (patient 4, magnification, × 200), highlights plasma cells. F H&E section (patient 4, magnification, × 200) showing muscle with mild perimysial inflammation (black arrow)
in_text_mentions: H & E sections revealed inflammation that preferentially involved the fascia extending to the perimysium and fascial thickening (Fig. 3).
